summary: Discovery call where Halcyon Finance evaluated Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. Primary concerns: predictable throughput for real-time scoring, data isolation (VPC/on-prem considerations), burst handling during end-of-month peaks, and security compliance (SOC 2 / KMS). Agreed next steps: sizing/pricing proposal, security deep-dive, and 1-day benchmark on customer sample workload.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining uh we got about 45 minutes on the cal, appreciate you all making time. quick intros?
[00:12] Mark Holloway (Halcyon, CTO): Mark here, Sana, Liam, Priya, Ethan - thanks. our goal today is to understand dedicated reserved capacity, isolation options and how burst would work for our month-end load spikes.
[00:27] Jordan Patel (Redwood SE): hi all, Jordan from infra/SE. i'll walk through how dedicated pools operate and then we can dig into sizing. bear with me, i've got a couple of slides - shared now.
[00:42] Sana Iqbal (Halcyon): quick context - we do real-time fraud scoring, model's ~13B, peak qps around 350 qps end-of-month, baseline 80 qps; latency target 95th < 120ms. can Redwood hit that on dedicated?
[01:05] Jordan: yes, with the right instance mix and batching config. typically customers reserve a GPU pool sized for baseline throughput and add burst capacity - small hot-pool or on-demand instances - to handle spikes. we'll recommend a profile once we see token distribution.
[01:33] Ethan Cole (Halcyon, Infra): we also need VPC peering and strict network egress rules, plus customer-managed KMS for keys. can you run in our VPC or do you require traffic through Redwood control plane?
[01:50] Avery: good Q. Redwood Dedicated supports private VPC connectivity and private control plane options for enterprise customers; you can choose customer-managed KMS and there are audit logs exported to your SIEM. note - for on-prem there's an additional packaging step.
[02:10] Priya Nandakumar (Security): SOC 2 and ISO? encryption at rest and in transit?
[02:16] Jordan: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant, and support TLS 1.2+, encryption at rest with KMS integration. i'll send the security pack after this call. sometimes transcripts say "Redwood dedicator" - ignore that, haha.
[02:31] Mark: pricing aside, the big unknown is how burst will behave. at 350 qps we can't afford 2s tails. what's the architecture for burst?
[02:46] Jordan: two patterns: 1) reserved pool sized for baseline with configured autoscale headroom for short bursts (warm GPUs in same pool) and 2) fallback to hosted spare capacity - automatically routed by policy. warm-up and kv-cache priming are key. for your model size 13B we recommend warm workers with continuous batching to keep latency stable.
[03:15] Sana: can you explain KV cache - we call it K-V cash sometimes - how does that affect cold start?
[03:22] Jordan: kv cache stores prefix keys for long-running conversations; for scoring workloads you get a different effect - the cache helps when repeated contexts are reused. cold start impact is reduced by preloading weights and priming key-value cache; we can pre-warm based on sample traces.
[03:40] Mark: do you support quantized variants to save cost? some teams use 4-bit quant to halve GPU memory and costs.
[03:47] Jordan: yes, we support multiple quantization profiles and can recommend a model variant with minimal quality loss. For production we typically A/B test quantized model first in a canary.
[04:05] Liam Torres (Procurement): on contracts - reserved capacity is a monthly commit, right? what about burst billing?
[04:12] Avery: reserved is a monthly commit. burst can be configured as pre-purchased burst credits or pay-as-you-go on top. we'll outline both options in pricing.
[04:25] Priya: audit logs - how granular and retention? we need 12 months immutable logs for our regulator.
[04:32] Jordan: audit events include per-request metadata, model version, user/route, and we can export to S3 or your SIEM with retention policies up to several years in enterprise plans.
[04:45] Mark: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated set up? we have a go-live target Jan 15.
[04:52] Avery: typical lead is 4-6 weeks for Dedicated with VPC peering and security review; on-prem longer. if we start sizing and legal now, Jan 15 is plausible.
[05:06] Sana: are there any known degradation modes - like if your pool is saturated?
[05:12] Jordan: yes - automatic fallback policies route to compatible model variants or hosted capacity; you can set priorities (latency-first vs cost-first). we also support queueing with SLA-based timeouts.
[05:26] Mark: competitors - we've talked to Anthropic and a couple of infra vendors; how is Redwood different operationally?
[05:33] Avery: Redwood is production-first - unified runtime and observability, transparent per-token breakdown, and strong defaults for batching / caching. important for ops teams to debug tail-latency.
[05:46] Liam: procurement question - do you require a PO to start pilot?
[05:50] Avery: small pilots can start on hosted with a credit; Dedicated pilots usually have a light contract or an MSA + SOW. we'll work with legal to streamline.
[06:05] Jordan: for benchmarks we'd need a sanitized sample of your workload and network creds to spin up a test in a reserved pool for one day; results include throughput, p95/p99, and cost estimates.
[06:20] Mark: sounds good. can you share a sizing template?
[06:23] Avery: yes - i'll share the sizing/pricing doc and Jordan will include the benchmark checklist.
[06:30] Priya: for the security call, Priya here - i'd like to deep-dive into KMS integration and audit export - propose times.
[06:38] Jordan: noted - we'll propose 2 slots next week.
[06:42] Sana: one more - deployment isolation: we want tenant isolation per environment and strict RBAC for routes.
[06:49] Jordan: Dedicated supports isolated GPU pools per tenant and RBAC via SSO (SAML/OIDC) and route-level permissions.
[06:58] Mark: ok recap - action items, send pricing/sizing, security pack, benchmark plan, propose security meeting.
[07:06] Avery: yep i'll follow up with a single email with attachments and proposed slots. thanks everyone.
[07:12] Meeting end.
